doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Church, spirituality and Expansions
summary: The church and gospel upbringing led him to Eastern philosophy and the message of Expansions: peace and harmony.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: That’s terrific. Your family I guess was, is it fair to say your family was religious?
So was there a spiritual thread throughout your life that stayed with you and when you became a leader what role did it play in the music you created?

That was it. Because you know people don’t realize the church is very important, you know, for us I guess as black people, because even with Trane, his father and grandfather was preachers. Aretha Frank— that church, you grow up in it and the music is fantastic and so what I did was, you know, I took that spirituality and all of a sudden I became aware of Eastern philosophy and different religions and I started studying them and then you find out, well wait a minute, all religions and all philosophies are basically saying the same thing. Everybody wants peace, harmony and enlightenment. So I said well why are we doing all the wars and fighting each other. And I started writing, the first time I wrote [inaudible] was on “Expansions.” And that’s when I said expand your mind so we can have a vision of a new world where everyone would live in peace and harmony. You know a good example is what happened last Wednesday [January 6, 2021]. You know we were having all this craziness going on and so I just took that spirituality from that, from the Baptist church, and just kept expanding it to a whole universal consciousness.
